text: Doing the DBF NULL hardening Codex drafted (owner-approved: tests + memo scrub + secure clear). Findings first: on current v1-development a nulled C/N/D/L/I value is ALREADY blanked in the .dbf slot (VFP does this too) - now pinned by tests. Real gaps: (1) the memo branch of replace_record_field_value_impl ignored is_null, so a nulled memo never got its _NullFlags bit and the old text stayed in the .fpt; (2) memo overwrite/ADDITIVE leave the superseded FPT block readable (VFP does too until PACK MEMO). Fix: memo null clears the pointer + sets the bit; superseded block payload is zero-filled unless another record references it (COPPERFIN_DBF_MEMO_SCRUB=0 restores VFP leave-in-place); whole-table/memo working buffers of a NULL/memo replace are wiped with a new non-elidable copperfin::security::secure_clear (best-effort, NOT a wipe-on-free policy). Not done, documented in docs/80: index keys, deleted-unpacked rows, other memo writers, copies elsewhere in memory, on-disk backups. Fail-first: 5 failures (all memo paths) before, 0 after in test_dbf_null_hardening.
